question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-555 (Remote Services with Stolen Credentials) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

anchor_names.name: Remote Services with Stolen Credentials
anchor_names.description: This pattern of attack involves an adversary that uses stolen credentials to leverage remote services such as RDP, telnet, SSH, and VNC to log into a system. Once access is gained, any number of malicious activities could be performed.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-593 (Session Hijacking) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

anchor_names.name: Session Hijacking
anchor_names.description: This type of attack involves an adversary that exploits weaknesses in an application's use of sessions in performing authentication. The adversary is able to steal or manipulate an active session and use it to gain unathorized access to the application.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-639 (Probe System Files) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

anchor_names.name: Probe System Files
anchor_names.description: An adversary obtains unauthorized information due to improperly protected files. If an application stores sensitive information in a file that is not protected by proper access control, then an adversary can access the file and search for sensitive information.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-21 (Exploitation of Trusted Identifiers) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

anchor_names.name: Exploitation of Trusted Identifiers
anchor_names.description: An adversary guesses, obtains, or "rides" a trusted identifier (e.g. session ID, resource ID, cookie, etc.) to perform authorized actions under the guise of an authenticated user or service.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-644 (Use of Captured Hashes (Pass The Hash)) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

anchor_names.name: Use of Captured Hashes (Pass The Hash)
anchor_names.description: An adversary obtains (i.e. steals or purchases) legitimate Windows domain credential hash values to access systems within the domain that leverage the Lan Man (LM) and/or NT Lan Man (NTLM) authentication protocols.
anchor_names.label: AttackPattern

question: Which ATT&CK techniques does CAPEC-652 (Use of Known Kerberos Credentials) map to, and what mitigations apply to those techniques?

anchor_names.name: Use of Known Kerberos Credentials
anchor_names.description: An adversary obtains (i.e. steals or purchases) legitimate Kerberos credentials (e.g. Kerberos service account userID/password or Kerberos Tickets) with the goal of achieving authenticated access to additional systems, applications, or services within the domain.
